chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Suleiman al-Hammar, from Bureyd al-Ajaly, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whose back was broken so that he could not sit, that regarding it is the complete wergild.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for the complete wergild (diya) when a person's back is broken and they cannot sit?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential precision of Imam Ali (AS) in categorizing injuries, specifically ruling that a broken back preventing sitting warrants the complete wergild (diya al-kamil). It underscores the Shia emphasis on functional impairment as a key determinant in compensation, reflecting the practical application of Quranic principles of justice in early Islamic legal history.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Suleyman Al Hammar, from Bureyd Al Ajaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who broke his back, so he was not able to sit, that regarding it is the (complete) wergild’.
